<a id="p172-a-p172-b--station-control-and-the-seifert-service-exchange"></a>

## Station control and the Seifert service exchange

**Sources on this page:** p172 A, p172 B.

**Related source pages:** [p168 A](168.md#source-p168-a), [p168 B](168.md#source-p168-b), [p169 A](169.md#source-p169-a), [p174 B](174.md#source-p174-b), [p174 C](174.md#source-p174-c), [p174 D](174.md#source-p174-d), [p174 E](174.md#source-p174-e).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-station-control-and-the-seifert-service-exchange"></a>


[Source certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/seifert_records.json)

**Nine source records, seven message groups.** The 7–9 November and 10–12 November published keys recover a sequence of radio-station reports and short service messages. Two pairs are repeated transmissions. These records are outside the original 22-entry challenge; the open p170 challenge is section **A**, not any of these neighboring records.

Source transcription, cipher checks and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The station-control interpretations of p168 A and B were already published by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**; their author manuscript discusses both on printed p23 / PDF page 24. The keys retain their recorded historical and modern provenance. This page provides a source-level edition, without claiming a first historical decipherment.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

The paired monitoring orders each gain their hundreds digit: **500**. Both physical receptions have the same complete ciphertext; repetition preserves the value once the shared square is interpreted. No source coordinate is changed. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Sofort US 500 hoeren.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p172_B, conditional shared square; 20/20 fixed positions:**

```text
SOFORTXUSX500XHOEREN
```

**Edited output — p174_D, conditional shared square; 20/20 fixed positions:**

```text
SOFORTXUSX500XHOEREN
```

</details>


<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-read-the-messages"></a>

### Read the messages

The prior body credit for p168 A also applies to its repeated content at
**p169 A**. Identification of the repeat, its exact coordinate differences,
and the present source edition remain our contribution.

Square brackets mark supplied letters or abbreviation expansions. Punctuation, capitalization and word spacing are editorial.

| Source | Readable German | Meaning and exact qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **p168 A**; repeated with errors at **p169 A** | Stehe ab 2200 unter Aufsicht Sol[d]atenrats. Stat[ion und] Personal fest in meiner Hand. Betrieb unverändert. Seifert. | From 22:00 the sender is under the soldiers' council's supervision; station/personnel remain firmly under his control and operation is unchanged. All 92 raw positions of p168 A decode exactly; the source spells `SOLATENRATS` without `D`. The connecting words in the `STATPERSONAL` expansion are editorial. |
| **p168 B** | Soldatenrat Cöln wird bald Funkstelle besetzen. Versucht schon Funksprüche aufzugeben. | Cologne's soldiers' council is expected to occupy the radio station and is already trying to submit radio messages. The raw text has `SOLDATENRA9` and `SCKON`; the readable version requires two explicit coordinate substitutions. |
| **p172 A** | Akten [s]ämtlich vernichtet. Schlüssel in pers[önlicher] Obhut noch vorhanden. Seifert. | All records have been destroyed; the cipher keys remain in personal custody. The source fixes 67/68 plaintext positions. One invalid printed glyph leaves the initial letter of `SAEMTLICH` unresolved; `S` is a supported reading, not a source-observed letter. |
| **p174 B** | Wenn Seifert eingetroffe[n], bitte Nachr[icht]. TOF. | Please report when Seifert has arrived. The source fixes 36/37 positions. One doubtful glyph permits `N`; a `G` interpretation of that glyph instead produces separator `X` after the raw spelling `EINGETROFFE`. `TOF` is not expanded. |
| **p174 C** | Wann Rückkunft Seifert? RE. | When will Seifert return? All 24 plaintext positions decode exactly. `RE` remains unexpanded. |
| **p172 B / p174 D** | Sofort US ?00 hören. | An immediate listening instruction. The two 40-coordinate copies are identical. The unknown hundreds digit can be **5, 6, 7, 8 or 9** under a globally consistent completion of the published square. The role of `US` and the units of the number are not established. |
| **p174 E** | Seifert abgefahren. RENTE. | Seifert has departed. The raw text is `SQIFQRTABGEFAHRENXRENTE`; restoring the name requires two explicit `G → X` coordinate substitutions. `RENTE` is retained literally. |

The shared surname connects the service records, but the surviving headers do not establish Seifert's full name or a complete itinerary. The printed time expressions are preserved in the certificate, including the anomalous `17.28 p.m.` in p174 E. The day digit in p172 B is overtyped; the identical p174 D copy is explicitly dated 12 November.

### Raw decipherments

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p168-a--184-coordinates--92-positions"></a>

#### p168 A — 184 coordinates / 92 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
STEHEAB2200UNTERAUFSICHTSOLATENRATSXSTATPERSONALFESTINMEINERHANDXBETRIEBUNVERAENDERTXSEIFERT
```

</details>

No cipher correction is required. Supplying `D` in `Soldatenrats` and expanding `STAT` are editorial reading choices only. The source is available in the [p168 A/B excerpt](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p168_AB.png).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p168-b--160-coordinates--80-positions"></a>

#### p168 B — 160 coordinates / 80 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SOLDATENRA9XCOELNXWIRDBALDFUNKSTELLEBESETZENXVERSUCHTSCKONFUNKSPRUECHEAUFZUGEBEN
```

</details>

At zero-based ciphertext positions **89** and **141**, `F → V` and `G → X` give `SOLDATENRAT` and `SCHON`. The other **158 coordinates remain unchanged**. These are proposed source emendations, not alternative square assignments.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p172-a--136-slots--68-positions"></a>

#### p172 A — 136 slots / 68 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
AKTEN?AEMTLICHVERNICHTETXSCHLUESSELINPERSOBHUTNOCHVORHANDENXXSEIFERT
```

</details>

The [source](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p172_AB.png) prints `DAAGC`: its final `C` is outside the ADFGVX alphabet and becomes one erasure at ciphertext position **119**. The plaintext domain at position **5** is exactly `{F,I,K,N,O,S}`. Filling that coordinate with `G` gives `S` and preserves all **135 valid received coordinates**. `PERSOBHUT` is retained; the readable expansion is *pers[önlicher] Obhut*.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p174-b--74-slots--37-positions"></a>

#### p174 B — 74 slots / 37 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFE?BITTENACHRXTOF
```

</details>

The [source excerpt](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p174_BCDE.png) shows a `C`-like or defective `G` glyph at the start of group `CVXXF`, ciphertext position **20**. Its conservative analysis is `?VXXF`. The uncertain plaintext position **22** has domain `{1,5,6,7,8,9,E,N,V,X}`.

The readable `N` completion uses **D** at the source erasure and preserves all **73 certain coordinates**. Reading the doubtful glyph as **G** instead gives:

**Conditional interpretation — alternate G reading of the doubtful source glyph:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFEXBITTENACHRXTOF
```

Within that single-source analysis, both alternatives are retained; the complete word `EINGETROFFEN` is an editorial inference.

An independent [p183 B witness](183.md#edition-cases-radio-nov12-arrival-departure-and-car-p183-b)
now supplies observed `D` at source index 20 and therefore `N` at plaintext
position 22. Together the two conservative source transcriptions support
every target pair. The original C/G-like appearance and its G-reading
alternative remain in the earlier certificate and source analysis above.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p172-b--p174-d--40-coordinates--20-positions-each"></a>

#### p172 B / p174 D — 40 coordinates / 20 positions each

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

```text
SOFORTXUSX?00XHOEREN
```

Both copies have the same ciphertext. All 40 coordinates are legible; the unknown digit comes solely from an unassigned cell in the published 10–12 November square. The verifier constructs a full bijective square witness for **each** candidate digit 5–9. The duplicate therefore confirms the transmitted coordinates but does not select a digit.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-p174-e--46-coordinates--23-positions"></a>

#### p174 E — 46 coordinates / 23 positions

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
SQIFQRTABGEFAHRENXRENTE
```

</details>

Changing ciphertext positions **2** and **28** from `G` to `X` gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
SEIFERTABGEFAHRENXRENTE
```

</details>

The other **44 coordinates remain unchanged**. The two corrections restore the same name directly present in the surrounding service traffic; the original `Q`s remain part of the raw edition.

The [p183 C witness](183.md#edition-cases-radio-nov12-arrival-departure-and-car-p183-c) supports `X`
at source index 2, directly corroborating the second `E` of the name. Both

separately priced contextual repair in each. The joint complete-name
proposal costs three observed-coordinate substitutions.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-the-p169-a-repeat"></a>

### The p169 A repeat

[p169 A](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p169_A.png) carries the same `SY v GK`, `2000` and `RICHI-184` metadata as p168 A, with a later intercept time. It prints **185 coordinates**, including the six-character group `DGDGGX`.

Deleting either adjacent `G` at zero-based source position **158** or **159** gives the same 184-coordinate conditional layer and this raw decipherment:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional deletion of source 158 or 159; equivalent aliases retained:**

```text
STEHEAB2200UNTEYAUFSICHTSOLATENRATWXSTATPERSONALFESTINMEIKERHANDXBETRIEBUNVERAENDURTXSEIFERT
```

</details>

It supports the repeated-message identification but is less clean than p168 A. Both deletion aliases are recorded. The untouched odd-length source is retained and is never silently decoded after dropping its last coordinate.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-evidence-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence and reproduction

The [certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/seifert_records.json) contains all nine literal source transcriptions, original headers, partial keys, raw plaintext domains, cropped-image hashes and exact proposed edits. It applies the already published keys; no unknown square cell is fixed by the prose.

```sh
python experiments/p170_continuation/verify_seifert.py
python experiments/p170_continuation/verify_seifert.py --json
```

The independent verifier checks **913 source slots**, every source-preserving fill, the four explicit coordinate substitutions, the p169 deletion aliases, both identical service copies, and all five globally attainable digit readings. A local copy of the source PDF can additionally be bound by SHA-256 with `--pdf /path/to/childs.pdf`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-sources-and-priority"></a>

#### Sources and priority

- **J. Rives Childs collection:** printed pp168, 169, 172 and 174; PDF page 171, 172, 175 and 177 in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The certificate retains its hash and the exact section headers.
- **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker:** *Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*, [author manuscript](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf), printed p23 / PDF page 24. This earlier work explicitly identifies the p168 A/B station-control reports; it also credits Childs's wartime decipherment of the Cologne message. The present edition does not reassign that priority.
- **Published keys:** [key catalog](../../data/keys.json), entries `Nov7-9` and `Nov10-12`, retaining original table and solver provenance.

<a id="p172-c1-p172-c3--namur-arrival-cassel-transport-and-armistice-information-requests"></a>

## Namur arrival, Cassel transport and armistice-information requests

**Sources on this page:** p172 C1, p172 C3.

**Related source pages:** [p180 E](180.md#source-p180-e), [p181 B](181.md#source-p181-b).

<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-namur-arrival-cassel-transport-and-armistice-information-requests"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four surviving source bodies report an arrival at Namur, direct prompt transport arrangements to Cassel, and request the local armistice conditions again. The Namur telegram explicitly lacks its second part; its first and third parts are presented without bridging that gap. Literal office labels, an opaque transport field and source-length spellings remain visible.

<a id="source-p172-c1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-p172-c1"></a>

### p172 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) SY v ZM (13.40 p.m., November 10th); 1412 3 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-116`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> Major Kroeger. GHQU. Soeben mit RXABLASS Namur eingetroffen.

**Meaning:** The first surviving part names Major Kroeger and reports a recent arrival at Namur. The opening may address Kroeger, so the arriving person is not securely identified. GHQU and RXABLASS remain opaque labels. The surviving third part closes with Hpt. Mannstaedt, and the source explicitly marks part 2 as missing.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
MAJORKROEGERXGHQUXIOEBENXMITXXRXABLASSXNAMURXEINGETROFFENX
```

**Edited output** — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
MAJORKROEGERXGHQUXSOEBENXMITXXRXABLASSXNAMURXEINGETROFFENX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The native 116-slot first part is complete. The source explicitly prints “2 TL (Missing)” before the separately preserved third part; no second part is supplied or counted.
- IOEBEN to SOEBEN is an explicitly priced lexical proposal. GHQU and RXABLASS remain literal and unexpanded; ABLASS is not asserted to be a person's name. The opening could be an address, and no arriving subject is supplied.
- The printed time is 13.40 p.m. and is retained without conversion. No historical identity beyond the literal surname KROEGER is inferred.

<a id="source-p172-c3"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-p172-c3"></a>

**Meaning:** The surviving third part asks for a response on the preceding matter and closes with the literal signature Hpt. Mannstaedt. The intervening second part is absent from the printed source.

<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical round-trip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

### p180 E

**Source transcription — header:** `E) SY A v SY (10.09 p.m., November 12th); 10.45; RICHI-224`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> Lt. Bauman. STATON sofort marschbereit 0 sein fuer M?TRANSPORT Cassel. Abtransport so schnell wie moeglich regeln. Kommandeur.

**Meaning:** The instruction addresses Lt. Bauman, calls for immediate readiness to move, and directs transport to Cassel to be arranged as quickly as possible. The spelling STATON and the literal fields 0 and M? TRANSPORT remain unresolved; the specific transport type is not identified.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
LTXBAUMANXSTATONSOFORTXMARSCHBERECT0SEINFUERXM?TRANSPORTXCASSELXABTRANSPORTSOSCHNELSWIEMOEGLICHRE?ELNXKOMMANDEUR
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
LTXBAUMANXSTATONSOFORTXMARSCHBEREIT0SEINFUERXM?TRANSPORTXCASSELXABTRANSPORTSOSCHNELLWIEMOEGLICHREGELNXKOMMANDEUR
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The source contains 224 slots, including all final groups; no coordinate is inserted, removed or moved.
- STATON is retained without inserting the absent I of STATION. BAUMAN remains the literal surname with one terminal N.
- MARSCHBERECT0 to MARSCHBEREIT0, SCHNELS to SCHNELL and RE?ELN to REGELN are separately priced lexical changes. The literal 0 is not silently changed into a separator.
- The Nov13–15b published key is used because it yields the demonstrated reading; the printed 12 November date is retained as a different evidence layer.
- The unknown position in M?TRANSPORT comes from an unresolved square cell and remains globally coupled. Its label is not chosen from historical expectations.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-staatsbank-accounting-cheques"></a>

<a id="p172-d1-p172-d2--state-bank-accounting-request-and-dispatched-cheques"></a>

## State-bank accounting request and dispatched cheques

**Sources on this page:** p172 D1, p172 D2.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-staatsbank-accounting-cheques-state-bank-accounting-request-and-dispatched-cheques"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two-part message addresses Staatsbank Berlin, asks for an accounting amount connected to the Generalkriegskasse, and requests notice of arrival of dispatched cheques. It contains no recovered payment amount. The first part needs one explicitly modeled missing coordinate; the second part uses its complete native frame.

<a id="source-p172-d1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-finance-staatsbank-accounting-cheques-p172-d1"></a>

### p172 D1

**Source transcription — header:** `D) LP v NKJ (6.06 p.m., November 11th); VON UKS LP 2127 (9/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-198`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 198-coordinate frame after one modeled insertion; 95/99 fixed positions:**

```text
STAATSBANKBERLINXERBITTENDRINLICHOTFUNKSPRU?HFUERBEST?RREICHERABRECHNUNGBETRAGD?RGENE?ALKRIEGSKASSE
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions, 3 printed-mask fills and one additional-slot fill; the insertion remains conditional.**

```text
STAATSBANKBERLINXERBITTENDRINLICHSTFUNKSPRUCHFUEROESTERREICHERABRECHNUNGBETRAGDERGENERALKRIEGSKASSE
```

</details>

**Readable German — preserves the exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Staatsbank Berlin. Erbitten DRINLICHST Funkspruch fuer OESTERREICHER Abrechnung Betrag der Generalkriegskasse

**Meaning:** The first part addresses Staatsbank Berlin and asks urgently by radio for an accounting amount concerning the Generalkriegskasse. The proposed word OESTERREICHER is left unexpanded; it is not used to identify a person or prove an Austrian institutional connection. The request continues in part 2.

**Editorial limits:**

- The source has 197 slots against the printed 198, with the four-coordinate group ADAX. One additional modeled slot is required for the disclosed 198-coordinate frame.
- All five insertion boundaries around ADAX are retained. Boundaries 27 and 28 tie for the lowest observed-change cost under the stated word proposal and yield the same completed ciphertext; neither is asserted as the unique historical loss location.
- DRINLICHOT to DRINLICHST and BEST?RREICHER to OESTERREICHER are explicitly priced lexical proposals. DRINLICHST remains a source-length spelling without inserting a G.
- The two printed dashes in DVX-- and C-shaped glyph in ACAXA occupy source slots and are filled separately from the additional coordinate.
- The page heading says 10 November, this section's interception header says 11 November, and its originating line says 9/11. All three source layers are retained; the Nov7–9 key is unchanged.

<a id="source-p172-d2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-finance-staatsbank-accounting-cheques-p172-d2"></a>

### p172 D2

**Source transcription — header:** `D) LP v NKJ (6.06 p.m., November 11th); VON UKS LP 2127 (9/11) 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-204`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 204-coordinate frame; 97/102 fixed positions:**

```text
VOM18XBISENDEOOTOBERGEZAHLTENYAYKXFERNERA?KUNFTSANZ?IGEUEBERA??XGESANDTECHEKSXHAUPTWECHSE?AMT89240911X
```

**Edited output — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions, 4 printed-mask fills; no source coordinate inserted, removed or moved.**

```text
VOM18XBISENDEOCTOBERGEZAHLTENMARKXFERNERANKUNFTSANZEIGEUEBERAM?XGESANDTECHEKSXHAUPTWECHSELAMT89240911X
```

</details>

**Readable German — preserves the exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Vom 18 bis Ende October gezahlten Mark. Ferner Ankunftsanzeige ueber am ? gesandte CHEKS. Hauptwechselamt 89240911.

**Meaning:** The continuation concerns the amount of marks paid in the period represented by 18 through the end of October, and asks for notice of arrival of cheques dispatched on an unresolved date. The closing is Hauptwechselamt followed by the literal reference 89240911; that reference is not treated as the requested payment amount.

**Editorial limits:**

- The native 204-slot second part needs no length adjustment. OOTOBER to OCTOBER and YAYK to MARK are priced observed-coordinate changes; four printed dashes are filled explicitly.
- CHEKS is retained without supplying an extra letter. The footer 89240911 is not silently split into a date or interpreted as a currency quantity.
- The unresolved date-like position after AM is square cell VF, whose remaining domain is {5, 6}. The value is not inferred from the source date or the earlier baseline completion.
- No amount paid is recovered: the telegram asks for an amount. The first part and this continuation must not be read as reporting that the footer is a monetary total.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-staatsbank-accounting-cheques-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) reads **am 6. gesandte Cheks** in part 2. The opposite square gives am 5.; the selected date is conditional on the cross-period reference relation and adds no source repair.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-staatsbank-accounting-cheques-source-and-frame"></a>

### Source and frame

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p172 excerpt](../../experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/sources/p172_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/inputs.json) · [All coordinate and insertion certificates](../../experiments/staatsbank_accounting_cheques/certificates.json)

The source page heading says 10 November. Section D has an interception header dated 11 November and an originating line `VON UKS LP 2127 (9/11) 2 TLE`. The published Nov7–9 key is retained with its two unresolved square cells; none of these date layers is silently normalized.

The first part advertises 198 coordinates but contains 197 occupied slots. Its sixth group is the four-coordinate `ADAX`. The model adds one unknown coordinate at one of that group’s five boundaries. It does not add a complete plaintext letter or change the period key. The second part has exactly its advertised 204 positions.

| First-part insertion boundary | Observed substitutions for displayed proposal | Printed-mask fills | Additional-slot fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 25 | 4 | 3 | 1 |
| 26 | 3 | 3 | 1 |
| 27 | 2 | 3 | 1 |
| 28 | 2 | 3 | 1 |
| 29 | 3 | 3 | 1 |

All indices are zero-based. Boundaries **27 and 28 tie**, and inserting the proposed A at either side of the already printed A gives the same completed ciphertext. The primary display uses boundary 28. This equality leaves the precise loss location unresolved; a minimum against proposed German words is not a unique historical diagnosis. The native 197-coordinate diagnostic, including its unpaired intermediate coordinate and source provenance, remains in the certificate.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-staatsbank-accounting-cheques-joint-meaning-and-unresolved-labels"></a>

### Joint meaning and unresolved labels

Read together, the parts ask for a radio report of an accounting amount connected with marks paid by the Generalkriegskasse in the period represented by `18` through the end of October, followed by a request for arrival information about cheques. The prose does not turn the closing reference `89240911` into either a payment amount or a reconstructed date.

The proposed OESTERREICHER reading costs a source change and a separately disclosed erasure fill. Its administrative referent is unresolved. DRINLICHST and CHEKS remain source-length spellings; no omitted G or extra C is supplied as formatting. The question mark after AM is cell VF with domain `{5, 6}`. Choosing either digit would also constrain the other unresolved Nov7–9 square cell; no such historical assignment is made. Specifically, VF must be the opposite label from the three shared XA positions in the [p155 C1/C2 repetition edition](155.md#edition-cases-radio-nov7-eighth-part-repetition).

## p172 E — Namur order for Staedt to contact HPT V. Weiher; complementary source witness

**Edition context:** The Namur order: two witnesses for Staedt and Weiher.

**Related source pages:** [p171 C](171.md#source-p171-c).

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-the-namur-order-two-witnesses-for-staedt-and-weiher"></a>



**Source reconciliation and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two closely related transmissions instruct **Hauptmann Staedt in Namur**
to contact `HPT V. WEIHER` at an Etappen inspection. The latter is to receive
a detailed order by `11 VORM`; the message is signed `MJR KROEGER`.
The witnesses together support this 126-position reading:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — joint witness reconstruction under the stated same-message model:**

```text
HPTMANNSTAEDTNAMURXXBITTESICHMITHPTVXXWEIHERETAPPENINSP1INVERBINDUNGSETZENDERBIS11VORMAUSFUEHRLICHENBEFEHLBEKOMMTXXMJRKROEGERX
```

</details>

The anomalous **`INSP1IN`** and literal **`HPTVXX`** are retained. The
edition does not silently replace the `1` with a separator or insert letters
into the title abbreviation. The source spelling `STAEDT` is retained
without a new biographical identification.

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-the-two-physical-sources"></a>

### The two physical sources

Both are in Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view),
and use the unchanged published **Nov10–12** square and ranks.

| Witness | Source | Header | Received slots |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| p171 C | [Printed p171, PDF page 174](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/sources/p171_C.png) | `--- v SY (7.26 p.m., November 10th); 1800; RICHI-252` | 252, including four printed dashes |
| p172 E | [Printed p172, PDF page 175](../../experiments/namur_order_witnesses/sources/p172_E.png) | `SY v MAX (7.21 p.m., November 10th); RICHI----; (J'md)` before the received groups | 242, all valid coordinates |

The receiving time on E is five minutes earlier than C's. The edition
preserves both timestamps and does not infer an actual relay sequence.
The p171 page heading is 9 November, while C's own receiving timestamp
explicitly says 10 November.

C's direct reading is:

```

</details>

E's earlier OCR stream had only 235 positions and did not yield this

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional same-message 252-slot frame with ten absent leading coordinates:**

HPTMANN?1AEDTNA?URXXBIT?ESICHJI?HPTVXXW?IHERETA?PENINSP?I?VERBI?DUNGSET?ENDERBI?11VORMAUSFUEHRLICHENBEFEHLBEKOMMRXXPJRKROEGERX
```

The ten-coordinate leading loss is inferred from the relationship between

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-why-the-alignment-is-useful"></a>

### Complementary coordinate evidence

Aligning E's first received coordinate with C source index **10** compares
**238 jointly observed coordinates**: **227 agree** and **11 conflict**.
E supplies observed values for all four printed dashes in C, while C
supplies E's ten modeled missing leading values:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — ten leading coordinates supplied by the other witness:**

```text
DGAAV FADFD
```

</details>

This offset is the unique highest agreement fraction among the **87 relative
offsets with at least 200 jointly observed coordinate pairs**. The comparison
uses ciphertext values, without a language score. It is a finite alignment
check, not a statistical significance claim or a global exclusion of every
possible original length.

The name correction **`WEGHER→WEIHER`** is supported by an observed coordinate
in E, rather than merely by the familiarity of a surname. Conversely, C
supplies correct-looking word and name values where E has other errors.
Lasry et al.'s separate discussion of the neighboring p172 C/p175 A family
also mentions von Weiher; that is retained as prior context, not used to
claim a new identification of the officer in these two witnesses.

<a id="edition-cases-people-namur-order-witnesses-exact-reconciliation-cost-with-the-alternatives-retained"></a>

### Exact reconciliation cost, with the alternatives retained

For two aligned streams to represent one common ciphertext, at least one
observed coordinate must change at each of the **11 conflicts**. The
selected readable body needs exactly **six substitutions in C and five in
E**, meeting that lower bound. Four printed-dash fills in C and ten modeled
prefix fills in E are separately accounted for.

Every coordinate value in the selected common ciphertext is **observed in
at least one witness**. No new coordinate value is supplied solely from a
word guess. The evidence for its plaintext pairs is:

| Complete coordinate pair supporting a selected character | Positions |
| --- | ---: |
| Observed in both witnesses | 102 |
| Observed only in C | 14 |
| Observed only in E | 9 |
| One coordinate supplied by each witness | 1 |
| **Total** | **126** |

The mixed pair is the first `P` in `ETAPPEN`, plaintext position **47**:
C supplies working coordinate 5 and E supplies working coordinate 52.
Thus **125 of 126 whole pairs** are directly observed in one of the two
sources, and the remaining pair is covered coordinate by coordinate.

Minimum cost does not establish a unique original reading. Each conflicting
coordinate has two source-supported choices, yielding **2¹¹ = 2,048**
minimum-cost common coordinate streams under this fixed alignment. The
verifier enumerates all of them, checks the same total cost, and records
their ordered digest. The complete conflict table and selected choice bits
make every alternative reproducible. The readable body is an editorial
choice within that set, with `INSP1IN` left unrepaired.

| Witness | Literal source slots | Analysis-frame slots | Raw fixed labels | Edition labels | Known-coordinate substitutions | Printed fills | Modeled-prefix fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p171 C | 252 | 252 | 122 / 126 | 126 / 126 | 6 | 4 | 0 |
| p172 E | 242 | 252 | 115 / 126 | 126 / 126 | 5 | 0 | 10 |
| **Total** | **494** | **504** | **237 / 252** | **252 / 252** | **11** | **4** | **10** |

These are two physical witnesses of **one 126-position body**, not two
independent bodies totaling 252 distinct characters. There is no deletion,
source reordering or baseline-key change.
